answer.rationale:
The binding constraints are that the primary contract lapses in 14 days without auto-renewal, the incumbent has already refused to reopen price, and only the low-cost vendor's quote satisfies the 18% mandate. That eliminates negotiate_terms (memory_c4's mechanism is blocked this cycle), defer_decision (memory_c5 applied to a non-critical, month-to-month service; here deferral means an uncovered primary contract), and renew_incumbent (memory_c1 buys stability but misses the mandate outright). add_second_source (memory_c3) is attractive for the 94%-utilization, zero-buffer exposure, but it leaves the expiring primary contract unaddressed, and I only get one decision.

So memory_c2 is the load-bearing memory, and it is exactly the one I want the source record for. It reads as a clean success, but three things about it are unverified and decision-relevant: it describes 'last year,' so the price and capacity it reflects may be stale; 'onboarding was quick' may have happened against a line with slack rather than at 94% of committed volume; and 'invoicing stayed accurate' is an administrative signal that says nothing about allocation behavior under stress. If the archived record shows the switch was made at lower utilization or for a less critical part, the cost case survives but the delivery-risk case does not, and I would fall back to a short bridge extension plus dual-award at the next review.

Downstream value risk: the mandate is a cost number, and cost is the one dimension the low-cost vendor is measured on in memory. Optimizing to it can quietly trade away the continuity that memory_c1 and memory_c3 record as real. A hard cutover with no buffer converts a price win into a delivery exposure that would not show up until the first missed allocation. So I intend the switch as a phased, dual-run ramp rather than a clean replacement: qualify and ramp the low-cost vendor while holding a short overlap on incumbent supply, with explicit checkpoints on on-time delivery and allocation behavior before full volume moves. That keeps the second-source logic from memory_c3 alive inside the switch instead of postponing it.

I am not treating the archive pull as confirmation. If it strengthens memory_c2, I proceed at the ramped scale, not a broad rollout; if it undercuts it, the plan changes rather than being defended.
